land.text: the State of Honduras within the Federal Republic of Central America

predecessors.note: The Honduras page dates the separation to 5 November 1838; the Federal Republic of Central America page (as read for the republic's own dossier) gives 26 October 1838.

capitals.name: Comayagua
capitals.note: 'Comayagua was the capital of Honduras until 1880, when the capital moved to Tegucigalpa.'

correction.text: the State of Honduras from its separation from the Federal Republic of Central America on 5 November 1838

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1840 but the page dates the separation from the Federation to 5 November 1838 ('an independent republic ... since 1838'). The 1840 outline is reused.

114,698 km2 for 1840-1845 against the infobox 112,492 km2 (undated; ratio 1.02): the modern outline, Gracias a Dios included (69 of its 72 cells). The British protectorate over the Mosquito Kingdom of 1844 ('the British government declared a new protectorate over the Mosquito Kingdom', Mosquito Coast page) claimed the coast 'from Cape Honduras in the north'; Cliopatria takes the 21 eastern cells from Honduras only in 1846. The Bay Islands (2 cells), British-administered 'from early 17th century to 1850', are outside the shape.

109,076 km2 for 1846-1859: the 1840 outline without 23 cells of the eastern Mosquitia (21 in Gracias a Dios), which Cliopatria gives to the Mosquito Kingdom (1853-1859) under the British protectorate of 1844-1860. The page gives no date for a Honduran loss (page silent: confidence 1 in the ledger) and says that by 1859 Britain 'ceded the northern part of the Mosquito Coast to Honduras'; the ledger returns the land in 1859, a year before Cliopatria.

correction.text: the full outline with the Bay Islands returned by Britain in 1859

keyframe_review.note: 114,698 km2 for the single year 1860: the eastern Mosquitia is back (ledger 1859). The Bay Islands (2 cells), which the page says Britain 'returned' by 1859, are added to the outline from this year. The land north of the Coco River stays disputed with Nicaragua from 1869 to 1960 (ledger).

correction.text: the 1861-1894 outline with the Bay Islands

keyframe_review.note: 115,148 km2 for 1861-1894: two cells more than the 1840 outline (Gracias a Dios and Nicaragua's Atlantico Norte), rasterisation noise. Adds the Bay Islands. The 1860 Treaty of Managua 'transferred suzerainty over the Caribbean coast between Cabo Gracias a Dios and Greytown to Nicaragua'; the Mosquito Reserve was incorporated into Nicaragua on 20 November 1894.

correction.text: the 1895-1978 outline with the Bay Islands

keyframe_review.note: 114,698 km2 for 1895-1978. The northern bank of the Coco River was disputed with Nicaragua until the 1960 ICJ judgment ('The point was designated as the official Honduras-Nicaragua border by an award of King Alfonso XIII of Spain in 1906', 'confirmed by the International Court of Justice in 1960'); the shape draws it as Honduran throughout and the ledger carries the contest. Bay Islands added.

region.text: the State of Honduras on its modern outline

ledger.note: 1838: Honduras leaves the Federal Republic of Central America. The page dates the separation to 5 November 1838 and says Honduras 'has been an independent republic and has held regular elections since 1838'; the History of Honduras page says Honduras 'broke away from the Central American Federation in October 1838' and the federation's own page gives 26 October 1838.

region.text: the eastern Honduran Mosquitia, 21 cells of Gracias a Dios that Cliopatria draws in the Mosquito Kingdom, around Cape Gracias a Dios and the Coco River

ledger.note: 1846: the eastern Mosquitia leaves the Honduran outline. Cliopatria draws the 21 eastern cells in the Mosquito Kingdom; the page is silent on a Honduran loss and says only that 'the British government declared a new protectorate over the Mosquito Kingdom' in 1844 (infobox 'English and British protectorate (1638-1787, 1844-1860)').

region.text: the eastern Honduran Mosquitia, 21 cells of Gracias a Dios that Cliopatria draws in the Mosquito Kingdom, around Cape Gracias a Dios and the Coco River

ledger.note: 1859: Britain returns the northern Mosquito Coast. 'By 1859 British opinion was no longer supportive of their nation's presence in the Mosquito Coast'; 'The British government returned the Bay Islands and ceded the northern part of the Mosquito Coast to Honduras' (the page does not name the Wyke-Cruz treaty); Cliopatria returns the cells in 1860. The 1860 Treaty of Managua, 28 January 1860, gave the coast from Cabo Gracias a Dios to Greytown to Nicaragua.
1859: the Bay Islands come back. The page says that by 1859 Britain 'returned the Bay Islands'; the Honduras page has the British administering them 'from early 17th century to 1850'.

region.text: the eastern Honduran Mosquitia, 21 cells of Gracias a Dios that Cliopatria draws in the Mosquito Kingdom, around Cape Gracias a Dios and the Coco River

ledger.note: 1869: the northern bank of the Coco River is disputed. 'Attempts to decide the sovereignty over the northern bank of the Wanks/Coco River' began in 1869 and the dispute lasted until the ICJ ruled for Honduras ninety-one years later. A boundary dispute, not a campaign; the 21 cells are the researcher's reading of the Honduran Mosquitia.

1880: the capital moves from Comayagua to Tegucigalpa. 'Comayagua was the capital of Honduras until 1880, when the capital moved to Tegucigalpa'; the History of Honduras page has President Marco Aurelio Soto move it.

region.text: the eastern Honduran Mosquitia, 21 cells of Gracias a Dios that Cliopatria draws in the Mosquito Kingdom, around Cape Gracias a Dios and the Coco River

ledger.note: 1960: the court settles the northern bank. 'In 1960 the northern part was granted to Honduras by the International Court of Justice'; the Cape page: the 1906 award of King Alfonso XIII of Spain was 'confirmed by the International Court of Justice in 1960'.

region.text: the eastern Honduran Mosquitia, 21 cells of Gracias a Dios that Cliopatria draws in the Mosquito Kingdom, around Cape Gracias a Dios and the Coco River

ledger.note: 1960: Honduras receives the northern Mosquito Coast. 'In 1960, the northern part of what was the Mosquito Coast was transferred from Nicaragua to Honduras.'

region.text: the Swan Islands, handed by the United States to Honduras

ledger.note: 1971: the Swan Islands pass to Honduras. 'The United States handed the Swan Islands to Honduras on November 22, 1971, and Honduras began exercising sovereignty there on September 1, 1972.'

wars.name: Guatemalan invasion of Honduras of 1906
wars.outcome: Honduras 'resisted an invasion from Guatemala in 1906' under President Manuel Bonilla; the page records no change of border.
wars.note: The title is the researcher's. The History of Honduras page also has the Cuyamel Fruit Company extend its rail lines in 1917 'into disputed Guatemalan territory' and a 1920s border controversy, with no settlement date.

wars.name: Football War
wars.outcome: No change of border on the page: 'In 1969, Honduras and El Salvador fought what became known as the Football War', and 'on 14 July 1969, the Salvadoran army invaded Honduras'.
wars.note: The page dates the invasion to 14 July 1969, an OAS 'cease-fire which took effect on 20 July' and 'a withdrawal of Salvadoran troops in early August', but names no ground held, so no occupation event is recorded yet (gap: the Football War page should name the occupied towns).

certainty.note: The northern bank of the Coco River was disputed with Nicaragua from 1869 and the Mosquito Coast was under a British protectorate in 1844-1859; no page opened describes the frontiers with Guatemala or El Salvador.

The Nicaraguan frontier is the 1906 award confirmed by the ICJ in 1960 (terminal point 14 59.8 N, 83 08.9 W). The frontiers with Guatemala and El Salvador and the Gulf of Fonseca are not on any page opened here.

notes: Cliopatria's eight shapes are the modern outline (469 cells) with two exceptions: 1846-1859 loses 23 eastern cells to the Mosquito Kingdom and 1861-1894 adds two cells (noise). Not settled: (1) The Honduran loss of 1846 is not on any page; the 1844 British protectorate is, and the page's 'from Cape Honduras' claim is wider than the 21 cells Cliopatria draws. (2) The 1906 award, Nicaragua's 1912 rejection and the 1960 judgment are on thin pages: no area or date for the execution of the judgment; the pages disagree in shape: the Mosquito Coast page has the cape ceded to Honduras 'by 1859' and also a 1960 grant of 'the northern part' by the ICJ, and the ledger keeps both (a gain in 1859, a contest of the northern bank 1869-1960 and a gain in 1960 of the same 21 cells) because the two pages give no finer account; the republic-of-nicaragua dossier (another group) should be checked against it. (3) The Bay Islands (2 cells) are added by corrections to every shape from 1860 because the Cliopatria shapes omit them. (4) The History of Honduras page has no 1933 Guatemalan border settlement (only a 1920s controversy and the 1917 rail incursion), no 1980 treaty or 1992 ICJ judgment with El Salvador and no date for the Nicaraguan award; those frontiers are the modern lines (page budget: five pages, two of them thin). (5) UPCA gives 26 October 1838 for Honduras' secession, the History of Honduras page 'October 1838', the Honduras page 5 November 1838. (6) The Swan Islands (gain of 1971) have no entry in the gazetteer; the event names them as a region. Names the gazetteer lacks: 'Swan Islands' (region); 'mosquito-kingdom' and 'republic-of-nicaragua' are dossiers of another group (am-08).
